items.title: StrategyGen awarded CMS contract to provide No Surprises Act Selected Dispute Resolution Services - OrangeSlices AI
items.reason: This item concerns CMS contracting decisions for implementing the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution process, which directly affects how balance-billing disputes are administered and impacts revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: StrategyGen has been awarded a CMS contract to provide Selected Dispute Resolution (SDR) services under the No Surprises Act. The SDR process is a key component of the Act's Independent Dispute Resolution mechanism, which handles disputes between payers and providers when they cannot agree on payment amounts for out-of-network care. This contract award affects how healthcare organizations will engage with the federal dispute resolution infrastructure and has implications for revenue-cycle teams managing balance-billing compliance and appeals processes.

items.title: More Clarity on the Horizon for Medicare Advantage Prior Authorization, Burden Will Remain - Medicare Rights Center
items.reason: Medicare Advantage prior authorization policy affects payer operations and provider claims processing; however, the item appears to be opinion/analysis rather than reporting a specific lawsuit, enforcement action, regulatory ruling, or sanction.
items.summary: The Medicare Rights Center discusses ongoing developments in Medicare Advantage prior authorization requirements, noting that while some clarity may emerge, administrative burden on providers will persist. The article addresses payer policies governing prior authorization procedures that impact claims submission and approval workflows. This is relevant to revenue-cycle teams managing Medicare Advantage claims, though the item does not report a specific enforcement action, court ruling, or regulatory sanction against a particular payer.
